moves.headline: Sandisk jumps 16% as beaten-down memory stocks rebound after the Thanksgiving break
moves.summary: Sandisk rose 16.0% to $85.36 in Friday's shortened session, leading a rebound in memory and storage stocks after a steep November sell-off. Micron gained about 7.6%, and a Kioxia demonstration of flash storage extending GPU memory for Nvidia systems added to the move.
why: The memory group had been hit hard through November as worries about AI data-center spending spread across chip stocks; Sandisk had lost roughly half its value over the previous month and about three quarters from its June peak. On the first session after Thanksgiving, buyers returned across the group, with Micron, Western Digital and Seagate also higher.

Kioxia, Sandisk's manufacturing partner in NAND flash, showed a large flash-storage setup working as extra memory for an Nvidia AI rack, which pointed to another use for flash in AI servers. The demo came with no orders or pricing, and on the same day TrendForce said conventional DRAM contract price increases could narrow through 2027, so the rebound came alongside an open question about how long memory prices stay high.

moves.headline: Sandisk drops 16% on its first full day of post-split trading as memory stocks crash
moves.summary: Sandisk shares fell 16.1% to $79.24, on the first trading day after its 8-for-1 stock split, as the AI sell-off hit memory makers hardest. The move followed a slide in NAND flash stocks that had already taken the shares well below their July highs.
why: Sandisk’s 8-for-1 stock split took effect at the open on November 20, so the shares traded at a new, lower price that has no effect on the company’s value. The 16% fall that day was a real decline, driven by the same sell-off that hit Micron, Western Digital and Seagate as investors questioned how long the AI-driven shortage of memory and storage will last.

Sandisk had been one of the best-performing stocks since its spin-off from Western Digital in February 2025, rising more than 20-fold at its peak on soaring NAND flash prices. Shifting dynamics in the NAND market had already pulled the stock down sharply in November before the split.
context: On November 20 the Nasdaq Composite fell 5.3% and the S&P 500 3.7%, pushing the S&P 500 and the Dow into correction territory and wiping out the Nasdaq’s gain for 2026. Semiconductors led the fall, capping their worst week since 2001.
Split-adjusted, the November 19 close of $776.22 equals about $97 a share on the new basis, so the fall to $79.24 reflects the market move rather than the mechanics of the split.
